messages.author: ddd23bd4f39c34aa
messages.subject: MI with ordinal items
parts:
Dear all,

I’m testing the measurement invariance of a questionnaire with ordinal items (three categories). The fit of a model met equal thresholds and loadings is worse compared to the fit of a model with equal thresholds, loadings, and residuals:

Equal thresholds and loadings:
chisq.scaled  387.228
df.scaled     190.000
pvalue.scaled   0.000
rmsea.scaled    0.089
cfi.scaled      0.932
tli.scaled      0.925

Equal thresholds, loadings, and residuals:
chisq.scaled  395.578
df.scaled     205.000
pvalue.scaled   0.000
rmsea.scaled    0.083
cfi.scaled      0.936
tli.scaled      0.934

Although this is possible (it was also the case in the example of https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/194879_192b64ad567743d392b559d650b95a3b.html), I’m wondering if my syntax is correct. I’ve used the syntax below to assess the model with equal thresholds and loadings (for strict invariance ("thresholds","loadings") has been replaced with ("thresholds","loadings","residuals"):

mod.strict <- 'F1 =~ HCR_H3 + HCR_H4 + HCR_H5 + HCR_H7 + HCR_H8 + HCR_H10 +
HCR_C1 + HCR_C2 + HCR_C4 + HCR_C5 + HCR_R1 + HCR_R2 + HCR_R3 + HCR_R4  + HCR_R5
HCR_H10 ~~ c(NA,NA)*HCR_H8
HCR_H3 ~~ c(NA,NA)*HCR_H8'
strict <- measEq.syntax(
configural.model = mod.strict,
data = data,
ordered = c("HCR_H3", "HCR_H4", "HCR_H5", "HCR_H7", "HCR_H8", "HCR_H10", "HCR_C1",
"HCR_C2", "HCR_C4", "HCR_C5", "HCR_R1", "HCR_R2", "HCR_R3", "HCR_R4","HCR_R5"),
parameterization = "theta",
ID.fac = "std.lv",
ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",
group = "group",
group.equal = c("thresholds","loadings"))
summary(strict)
cat(as.character(strict))
strict <- as.character(strict)
strict <- cfa(strict, data = data, group = "group", ordered = c("HCR_H3", "HCR_H4", "HCR_H5", "HCR_H7", "HCR_H8", "HCR_H10", "HCR_C1","HCR_C2", "HCR_C4", "HCR_C5", "HCR_R1", "HCR_R2", "HCR_R3","HCR_R4","HCR_R5"), parameterization = "theta")

In addition, the modification indices of the strict invariance model (with a Bonferroni correction) are:
lhs  op     rhs block group level     mi    epc sepc.lv sepc.all sepc.nox p.value  bonf
80  HCR_H3 ~*~ HCR_H3     1     1     1 14.818 -0.595  -0.595       -1       -1       0 0.045
174 HCR_H3 ~*~ HCR_H3     2     2     1 14.818  0.631   0.631        1        1       0 0.045

However, I’ve used the Theta parameterization and, as I understood, scaling factors are only used in the Delta parameterization.

Kind regards,
Carlijn

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MI with ordinal items
parts:
The fit of a model met equal thresholds and loadings is worse compared to the fit of a model with equal thresholds, loadings, and residuals:

Equal thresholds and loadings:
chisq.scaled  387.228
df.scaled     190.000

Equal thresholds, loadings, and residuals:
chisq.scaled  395.578
df.scaled     205.000

It's exact fit is worse. 

Although this is possible

Not for exact fit.  Approximate fit (relative to df) indices behave differently, particularly when the increase in chi-squared is less than the increase in df.
I’m wondering if my syntax is correct
I’ve used the Theta parameterization and, as I understood, scaling factors are only used in the Delta parameterization.

Sort of.  In both parameterizations, the scaling factors and residual variances are both "there", but only one of them can be "used" in the syntax at a time.  In delta, scaling factors are fixed for identification but can be freed by setting other constraints; residual variances are simply functions of scaling factors and other parameters.  In theta, it is the reverse situation: residual variances are fixed for identification but can be freed by setting other constraints, whereas scaling factors are simply functions of residual variances and other parameters.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: MI with ordinal items
parts: I’m not sure what the suggestion of the modification indices (HCR_H3 ~*~ HCR_H3) indicates

I also find it surprising that they are considered to potentially free when parameterization = "theta".  But modification indices are just generally unintelligent quantities.  The algorithm is to simply take the parTable(fit) output, look for any fixed parameters, then calculate the index for it.  If you want to be more cognizant of the parameters you would be willing to free, you can pass them to lavTestScore() explicitly.  Then there will be fewer of them, and they will all make sense (because you chose them).
Other modification indices are not significant (with a Bonferroni correction):

You can't trust the p values here.  The robust correction available with lavTestLRT() is not available for score tests because you haven't actually fit the less-constrained model (that would be necessary to calculate the scale/shift parameters for the chi-squared / mod. index).  Rank order should generally be the same for the naive score statistics, but we don't know their distribution to calculate a p value.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
